text:
### Observed differences

- In the later window, A01 appears for the first time: it occurred in none of the 200 earlier traces but now runs in about 56 in 100 traces, about 2.4 times per trace on average (roughly four times in the traces that contain it), around the middle of the trace in event order (median position about 0.49), with its outgoing flow split almost evenly over four successors — A09 about 27 in 100, A02 about 25, A11 about 24, A05 about 23. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001]
- In the later window, A14 is no longer observed: earlier it ran in all 200 traces, always at the very end together with A03, the two closing each trace in a fixed order within each trace (A03 before A14 in about 52 in 100 traces, A14 before A03 in about 48); in the later window A03 is the final event of every trace (position 1.0 in all traces, no outgoing transitions observed). [OCC010, POS003, POS012, REL033, DIR003, DIR013]
- Routing into A01 changed: A09 and A13, which earlier led to A02 (about 58 and 50 in 100 of their outgoing transitions) and A11 (about 43 and 49), now lead exclusively to A01; A08, A10 and A17, which could not lead to A01 earlier, now do so in about 53, 53 and 58 in 100 of their outgoing transitions, with A06 taking most of the remainder. [DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR012, DIR016]
- The closing route changed accordingly: A06 earlier fed the closing pair (to A03 about 52 in 100, to A14 about 47) and now leads to A03 in every observed case, always one event position away where earlier about half were two positions away. [DIR006, REL052, LAG024]
- A05 appears in far fewer traces in the later window (about 29 versus 62 in 100; mean occurrences about 1.2 versus 2.0) and its wiring changed: A11 now leads to A16 (about 50 in 100) instead of to A05 (about 54), and A05 leads to A13 (about 49) instead of A16 (about 49). A12 also appears in fewer traces (about 20 versus 37 in 100). [OCC003, OCC008, DIR005, DIR011]
- Several activities run somewhat more often in the later window, for example A11 (about 70 versus 62 in 100 traces; mean about 2.3 versus 1.8), A16 (about 70 versus 62), A09 and A15. [OCC005, OCC007, OCC011, OCC012]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a control-flow restructuring in which A01 — absent from all 200 earlier traces — was added as a mid-process branching activity that now runs in about 56 in 100 traces and leads roughly equally often to A02, A05, A09 and A11, while A14, previously executed in every trace as the closing step together with A03, was removed, so that A03 now ends every trace and A06 always flows into it. The surrounding routing matches: A09 and A13 now lead only to A01, and A08, A10 and A17 lead to A01 in about half of their outgoing transitions. [OCC001, OCC010, POS001, POS003, POS012, DIR001, DIR003, DIR006, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR012, DIR013, DIR016, REL033, REL052]

Supporting signs: the two core shifts are all-or-nothing participation changes (0 versus 112 traces for A01; 200 versus 0 for A14, out of 200 traces in each window), the new and lost edges show up directly in the successor profiles, A01 co-occurs with every major activity only in the later window while A14 co-occurred with A03 and A06 in every earlier trace and in none afterwards, and the same picture recurs across the occurrence, successor, position, relation and distance indicators. Differences of this size lie beyond about 995 in 1000 random re-splits of these windows, so sampling variation between two 200-trace samples does not explain them. [OCC001, OCC010, DIR001, DIR003, DIR006, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR012, DIR013, DIR016, POS001, POS003, POS012, REL002, REL011, REL033, REL052]

Limitations: the evidence cannot show whether the appearance of A01 and the disappearance of A14 were one coordinated modification or two independent ones, and it reports no chance-expectation figures for the number of qualifying items, so the judgement rests on the size, directness and cross-family consistency of the differences; strictly, "not observed" means absence from these samples, though with 0 of 200 traces on one side a rare-variant explanation is implausible. [OCC001, OCC010]

Other differences: A05 appears in far fewer traces (about 29 versus 62 in 100) and was rerouted — A11 now leads to A16 instead of A05, and A05 leads to A13 instead of A16 — with A12 also appearing in fewer traces (about 20 versus 37 in 100), while A11, A16, A09 and A15 run somewhat more often; these may be downstream of the same restructuring, but the evidence does not tie them to the A01/A14 changes. [OCC003, OCC005, OCC007, OCC008, OCC011, OCC012, DIR005, DIR011]
